messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up from the fanout-compression RFC — we need to pick a pragmatic default for the schema-gate behavior before the sprint starts.
Maya: Do we have a short summary of the options?
Alex: TL;DR: 1) Strict schema-gate at ingress (reject or drop unknown attrs) 2) Lenient ingress + canonicalizer in pipeline 3) Compression transform that prunes unknowns but preserves a minimal provenance envelope. Each has cost/query tradeoffs.
Sanjay: Option 1 gives best query predictability but will block a lot of edge SDK versions. Ops overhead to coordinate rollout is non-trivial.
Irene: Option 2 seems safest for client compatibility, but increases storage and downstream enrichment cost. We'll need a stronger dedupe/compaction pass later.
Jess: Can we quantify the cost delta rough order-of-magnitude? e.g., +X% storage, +Y% ingest CPU for option 2 vs 3?
Alex: Rough numbers from prototype: option 2 ~ +18% storage, +12% CPU; option 3 (compress at ingress) ~ +6% storage, +4% CPU but needs a cache for provenance lookups which complicates fanout.
Luke: For cost attribution, compression at ingress loses some attribute lineage — hard to reconstruct which service added which attr for billing. That will impact tenant-level chargebacks.
Sanjay: We could keep a tiny breadcrumb envelope (3 fields: origin, SDK_version, attr_hash) to help attribution while still trimming payload. Small win on query/chargeback.
Irene: Breadcrumbs sound reasonable. How big would that be per event?
Alex: ~120 bytes avg. For 500M events/day that's ~60GB/day extra — not negligible but we could TTL breadcrumbs cheaply (7d) and only retain full lineage for sampled events.
Jess: Sampling lineage for full retention + lightweight breadcrumb for all seems like a pragmatic hybrid. Any gotchas?
Maya: One: queries that need full lineage for a non-sampled event will fail. Two: rollbacks when SDKs change attribute names — compression could permanently drop fields unless canonicalizer runs.
Sanjay: For SDK churn we should require a compatibility header in the breadcrumb: "compat-v" that lets the canonicalizer pick transformation rules. That lets us do safe prune + later rehydrate if needed.
Alex: Proposed decision: default to option 3 (ingress compression) + breadcrumb envelope {origin, sdk_v, attr_hash, compat_v} + 7d breadcrumb TTL + sampled full lineage retention (configurable per-tenant).
Irene: +1 if we add a migration playbook for SDK owners and an explicit deprecation window for attr removal.
Luke: I want an explicit note that chargeback queries may need a best-effort mode that falls back to sampled lineage with a warning tag.
Jess: I'll add the cost numbers and the fallback guidance to the RFC follow-up doc.
Alex: Thanks — next steps: Jess updates the doc, Infra outfits a small metadata TTL tier for breadcrumbs, DevEx emails SDK owners about compat header.
ops-bot: Reminder: schedule review meeting — /remind @eng-platform in 2 days to review updated RFC. :calendar:
Maya: Awesome — thanks all. I'll sync with DevEx on the email copy.
Alex: Closing thread — we'll land the decision in the RFC doc and track rollouts in the sprint board.
